date_note: Adene announced the intrusion on Monday 23 November, per articles published 24 November.
title: Adene says unauthorized intrusion took Portugal's energy certificate portal out of service
summary: Adene, which runs Portugal's building energy certification system, announced on Monday an unauthorized intrusion into its systems, according to EFE and El Periódico de la Energía. The national portal for energy certificate applications is out of service with no reopening date. Adene says it isolated the affected equipment, notified the National Cybersecurity Centre and the Judicial Police, and is investigating whether personal data was accessed. It says issued certificates remain valid.
plain: Portugal's energy agency Adene says an intruder got into its systems and its energy certificate application portal is down. It says issued certificates stay valid and it is checking whether personal data was accessed.
exec: Adene reports an unauthorized intrusion that put its energy certificate application portal out of service, with no reopening date; whether personal data was accessed is under investigation.
action: As Adene advises, distrust messages or calls asking for personal data or credentials in its name; Adene says it never requests passwords through those channels.

validation.note: El Periódico de la Energía and ABC Color (EFE) both relay Adene's statement and read alike, so they may share one wire text; Adene's own notice was not found or read.
